title: Gate: delivery_completeness_check resolves backlog items from the git repo root (0-completion bug)

decisions.note: HIL explicitly asked to fix the delivery-completeness ROOT/rel bug; design sha e75c8c4f4179 has 0 pending findings.

brief.problem: delivery_completeness_check silently reports 0 completions when product-forge is a subdirectory of the git root.
brief.what_adds: Repo-root-aware path resolution + fail-closed load + regression test.
brief.why_now: The evidence-based DoD gate is a no-op in this workspace.
brief.success: The gate counts real completions and a test proves it.

objective: Make the evidence-based delivery-completeness gate see real completion transitions in this git layout by resolving changed item paths from the git top-level, failing closed on malformed items, and proving it with a test.
acceptance_criteria: delivery_completeness_check.transitions() resolves each changed item path under `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` instead of joining it to product-forge/ROOT, so a committed in_progress->completed transition is detected and counted instead of silently skipped.

The path loader fails closed on an unreadable/malformed changed item (JSONDecodeError propagates) while a path deleted in the diff (FileNotFoundError) is skipped; the gate prints the real completion count.
A regression test in test-framework/tests/test_delivery_completeness.py proves repo-root-relative path resolution and transitions() detection using a temp repo root, and precheck stays green.
out_of_scope: Changing the placeholder/RCCA baseline semantics or the completion gate's policy.
Fixing other scripts with the same ROOT/rel pattern (audit separately).
approach: Add _repo_root() (git rev-parse --show-toplevel) and _load(rel) to delivery_completeness_check.py, mirroring gate0_check/gate1_transition_check; use _load(rel) in transitions(). _load returns {} only for FileNotFoundError and lets JSONDecodeError propagate (fail closed). Extend test_delivery_completeness.py with a temp-root test for _load and a monkeypatched transitions() detection test.

prior_decisions: BI-PF-1409 shipped delivery_completeness_check.py (evidence-based DoD) to block placeholder AC/verification on completion transitions.

gate0_check.py and gate1_transition_check.py already resolve changed backlog files from the git repo root via _repo_root()/_load(); BI-PF-1475 fixed gate0 for the same product-forge-subdirectory layout.
BI-PF-1248 (Tech Debt & Repo Hygiene) is the owning epic for gate gaps/script drift.
existing_path: scripts/dev/delivery_completeness_check.py:94 transitions() joins (ROOT / rel) where rel is repo-root-relative (product-forge/data/backlog/items/...), so it reads product-forge/product-forge/... and skips every completion.
scripts/dev/gate0_check.py:36 _repo_root() + _load() (fixed in BI-PF-1475) is the established pattern.
test-framework/tests/test_delivery_completeness.py covers placeholder/RCCA/baseline but not path resolution.
assumptions: `git diff --name-only` emits paths relative to the git top-level (PF-features), so joining them to product-forge/ROOT is always wrong in this workspace.
A completion transition is an existing item file whose status moved into completed/closed/done; a deleted item file is not a completion and should be skipped.
The gate runs from product-forge but must work for any clone layout where the git root is an ancestor.
divergences: The gate currently swallows JSON/IO errors into an empty dict; the fix narrows the catch to FileNotFoundError only, so malformed state fails closed.

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=e75c8c4f4179
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - The monkeypatched `transitions()` test proves detection logic only in isolation; it does not prove that `transitions()` actually consumes `_repo_root()` for changed-item paths (the exact regression being fixed). AC3 requires proving both together — a wiring regression (e.g. `transitions()` still joining against `product-forge/ROOT`) would keep the test green. Add at least one assertion that the path handed to the loader is repo-root-relative.
  - `_load` is now the third copy of the `_repo_root`/`_load` pattern (gate0_check, gate1_transition_check, delivery_completeness_check). Deferring the shared-helper extraction "to a separate audit" leaves three writers of a path-resolution/security-sensitive utility; register a single owner now (CL-001) even if the consolidation lands later.
MINOR:
  - Fail-closed is defined only for `JSONDecodeError`; `PermissionError`/other `OSError` still propagate as raw tracebacks with no item-path context, which hurts diagnosability at the gate. Catch-and-re-raise with the path logged (or log before propagating) would preserve fail-closed while meeting the observability bar.
  - `FileNotFoundError` skips are silent by design; if no metric/log records how many paths were skipped, a deleted-in-diff completed item can under-count transitions without any signal. Emit a debug/warn line with the skipped path count.
  - `_repo_root()` behavior when `git` is unavailable, the subprocess fails, or the tool runs outside a repo is unspecified (no timeout, no exit-code handling). Define fail-closed vs fallback explicitly; a hang on `git rev-parse` would block the whole precheck pipeline.
NIT:
  - `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` should be invoked with an argv list (no `shell=True`) and a timeout; document that assumption in the helper's docstring.
  - The temp-root test should also assert that a file outside the temp root is NOT resolved (path-escape guard), proving the resolution is strictly root-scoped.
SUMMARY:
  - Solid, low-risk, in-language tooling fix with a clear fail-closed posture and rollback; no data, authz, or tenant concerns (checklist items 3/4/8/9 are N/A and should be stated as such in the design, per CL-008).
  - Top risks: (1) the monkeypatched `transitions()` test can pass while the actual root-resolution wiring regresses — AC3 not yet demonstrably met; (2) third duplication of `_repo_root`/`_load` defers a reuse decision that should be owned now.
  - Require: one non-monotpatched wiring assertion, skip/permission observability, and a stated git-failure contract before Gate 2.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

sig:2c28b55a492c91ce.note: test_transitions_uses_repo_root monkeypatches only _git and _repo_root; transitions() calls the real _load, which resolves the item under the temp repo root. If transitions still joined ROOT/rel, _load would see a missing file and the test would return [] instead of BI-X, so the test fails on the exact regression.

sig:0ef8de232b912e6e.note: Extracting a shared repo-paths helper is a refactor across gate0/gate1/delivery-completeness; it is recorded as a BI-PF-1248 tech-debt follow-up. This item mirrors the established pattern and does not change the other gates.

sig:6b53405b732fedf8.note: _load catches OSError and JSONDecodeError and raises RuntimeError with the changed-item path, so PermissionError and parse failures are diagnosable and fail closed.

sig:5e4722fd69a6567d.note: transitions() counts skipped deleted paths and prints 'delivery-completeness: skipped N deleted path(s)' to stderr when N > 0.

sig:cc06f85e2fd6791b.note: _repo_root runs git with an argv list, a 20s timeout, and raises RuntimeError when git is unavailable or the cwd is not a repo (no silent fallback).

sig:8ac9851185173f27.note: Both git calls use argv (no shell=True); _repo_root has a 20s timeout and _git has the same.
